We are inviting Entrepreneurship Support Organisations (ESOs) in Bengaluru, India, and Nairobi, Kenya, to

We are inviting Entrepreneurship Support Organisations (ESOs) in Bengaluru, India, and Nairobi, Kenya, to apply for the Circular Economy & Social Impact Programme for ESOs and the opportunity to design and run their own circular economy programme for entrepreneurs.
Programme activities Selected organisations will join the Circular Economy & Social Impact Masterclasses running between late April and July 2026.
The learning modules draw on Climate KIC’s technical expertise and three years of hands-on experience supporting circular ventures in both ecosystems between 2023 and 2025.

Upon successful completion of the masterclasses, the ESOs are eligible to apply for a grant of up to 50.000 EUR (per city) to design and run a dedicated entrepreneurship programme focused on circular economy and social impact.
We accept applications from organisations (both for profit and non-profit), that actively support ventures and entrepreneurs through support programmes such as incubators and accelerators.

Eligible organisations need to showcase a strong motivation to work on climate innovation, circular economy and social impact and a strategic vision on how these aspects are being (or will be) implemented in the organisation.

Geographic eligibility: We welcome applications from India and Kenya with a specific focus on ESO’s supporting ventures in Bengaluru and Nairobi. *More details on eligibility criteria can be found in the open-call documen t.

Catalyse NEB is the EIT Community New European Bauhaus accelerator for start-ups integrating sustainability, aesthetics and inclusion into their businesses, products and services. Built on the foundation of the New European Bauhaus (NEB) – Europe’s creative engine for turning the Green Deal into everyday reality, rethinking how we build our cities, produce materials, and shape communities – Catalyse NEB helps you scale your business and your purpose, while connecting you to Europe’s most vibrant innovation community.

That includes angel investors looking to invest in our start-ups, corporates looking for novel solutions to their challenges and institutional investors looking to invest in large-scale city transformations. Register your interest with us via this form so our investment team can understand your priorities. Register here Investing for 1.5C To solve complex problems, you need to look at things differently. Climate KIC is bringing systems thinking to our investment activity to develop a new way of thinking about investing in a better tomorrow. Climate KIC partners closely with a
Climate KIC partners closely with a select group of committed impact investment funds via our Investing for 1.5C initiative.
Almanac Ventures and UnaTerra are founding partners in the initiative and work with us daily to advance climate action.
Climate KIC leads the initiative and provides the partners with deal flow, strategy support, climate impact services, and growth support to portfolio companies.

At the same time, Almanac Ventures and UnaTerra each bring a unique focus on a different aspect of the climate innovation journey by looking at a particular sector, geography, or stage of development.
Our founding partners Almanac Ventures are on the hunt for bold Deeptech solutions — real scientific breakthroughs — that can decarbonise industrial sectors and supply chains.

Almanac Ventures mission is to make a real, positive impact on the climate while backing ventures that are financially sustainable, wildly scalable, and primed for killer returns in the future economy.

Since its inception – using the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) as a blueprint for our investment strategy – they have been helping to create the next generation of industry leading impact businesses dedicated to solving the world’s toughest challenges, starting with preserving and restoring biodiversity while also mitigating climate change.

Una Terra’s ambition is to not only invest capital, but also provide direct support and capabilities, education and leadership to companies that want to transform entire industries with commercial technology and innovation, with asset-light models that can be scaled through marketing, commercial introductions, partnerships, new market entry and accelerated go to market.

Investing for 1.5C partner – a full scale and long-term partnership between Climate KIC and investment fund managers interested in strategic decarbonisation opportunities.

The Climate KIC Academy is our capability-building arm under which we build the skills, mindsets and networks necessary to drive the green transition towards a fair and just future within planetary boundaries. It aims to equip leaders with both technical and transversal skills needed to navigate the complex challenges of climate change. Why does it exist? The Climate KIC Academy exists to address the critical shortage of skilled leaders who can effectively collaborate, innovate, and lead in the climate sector. While the technology and ideas are available,
The academy is designed to fill this gap and prepare individuals to lead the global climate movement.
The duration of the Climate KIC Academy programme varies depending on the specific course or pathway chosen.

Partially yes, the Climate KIC Academy is delivered primarily following a hybrid approach through live workshop experiences (online or in-person) complemented by self-paced e-learning training modules.
We do have self-paced courses, mini-courses and micro-credentials as part of Climate KIC Academy wider offering, together with more lengthy and interactive services.
The primary language of delivery for the Climate KIC Academy is English.
The EIT Label is the European Institute of Innovation and Technology’s quality certificate for education.
The Climate KIC Academy has been awarded the EIT Label for non-degree programmes.
FAQs for Learning Partners How can our organisation partner with the Climate KIC Academy?
Partners benefit from early access to innovative solutions and enhanced visibility within the climate action community.
What benefits do partners gain by collaborating with the Climate KIC Academy?
Climate KIC is Europe’s leading climate innovation agency and community, bridging the gap between climate commitments and current reality.

By collaborating with the Climate KIC Academy, partners gain the opportunity to be at the forefront of climate innovation together, engaging with a global network of leaders and experts dedicated to driving meaningful climate action.

The aim of this call is to select from Mission Cities a cohort of Pilot Cities, which will explore and test pathways to accelerated change towards 2030 climate neutrality goals — relevant to a city’s key emission domains — and to generate accelerated learning that can inform subsequent replication and scaling

The aim of this call is to select from Mission Cities a cohort of Pilot Cities, which will explore and test pathways to accelerated change towards 2030 climate neutrality goals — relevant to a city’s key emission domains — and to generate accelerated learning that can inform subsequent replication and scaling efforts in all other EU cities.

Only local authorities or city administrations selected to be part of EU Mission for climate-neutral and smart cities by 2030 (Mission Cities) are eligible to apply to, and receive funding under, this Call.
In the case of a group of cities applying together in one proposal, the size of the requested subgrant must follow the award amounts as stated in the Call Guidelines.

These organisations could be, for example: research institutions, universities, SMEs, NGOs, associations, citizen groups or other relevant stakeholders involved in the implementation of the climate ambitions of a Mission City participating in the consortium.

Activities eligible for funding are: Pioneering activities to support climate-neutrality, including the deployment of innovative (new or improved) technology, product, process, service, solution, policy, or governance model at city level, explored in a cross-sectoral and systemic manner.
These innovations shall account for co-benefits (e.g., health promotion) and the “Do No Significant Harm” (DNSH) principle.

Activities to support climate-neutrality to establish new knowledge and build capacity and capabilities of city government and associated local actors through training, workshops, and other forms of learning.

Activities aiming to build more collaborative communities, to advance new governance models at city level, and to engage citizens (including vulnerable/marginalised groups) and enable them to act on climate change in a systemic and cross-sectoral manner.

The experiment aims to address the economic and social disempowerment of women due to the lack of mobility by exploring the impact of e-mobility solutions on their lives and the factors that can make the e-mobility network robust by strengthening the local ecosystem. The project seeks to experiment with the e-mobility network as an investible model for replication in other districts or states across India. The experiment aims to combine inclusive participation, community-led communication, and diverse social, digital, and agro-ecological technologies to promote transformational change in the organic waste systems of municipalities. It also seeks to connect existing initiatives and inspire collaboration for sustained change. Additionally, the project aims to investigate how this learning experiment can connect with the cycles of other systems, particularly the local electoral system, to support transformational change.
